paper.title: BIP-0173: Base32 address format for native v0-16 witness outputs, and BIP-0350: Bech32m format for v1+ witness addresses (format specifications with published test vectors, not peer-reviewed papers)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the BIPs' prose (string structure, 32-character table, BCH checksum over GF(32) with the generator constants, final xor 1 or 0x2bc830a3, 5-bit to 8-bit conversion rules, segwit address rules); the BIPs' Python reference code and the Bitcoin Core code were not copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: BIP-173: 7 valid Bech32 strings are accepted as Bech32 and rebuilt exactly by the encoder (7 of 7); 12 invalid strings are rejected, each with the published reason class (12 of 12)
BIP-173: 6 valid segwit addresses decode to the published scriptPubKey hex (6 of 6); 10 invalid addresses are rejected with the published reason class (10 of 10)
BIP-350: 7 valid Bech32m strings accepted as Bech32m and rebuilt by the encoder (7 of 7); 14 invalid strings rejected with the published reason class (14 of 14)
BIP-350: 8 valid segwit addresses (witness versions 0 to 16 rules) decode to the published scriptPubKey hex (8 of 8); 15 invalid addresses rejected with the published reason class (15 of 15)
Every valid Bech32 string decodes only as Bech32 and every valid Bech32m string only as Bech32m (7 of 7 and 7 of 7), as BIP-350 states

expected_values_source.what: the test-vector sections of BIP-0173 and BIP-0350; vectors.inc is generated from the fetched BIP text by a script (strings with the few raw non-ASCII bytes spelled as octal escapes, reasons, scriptPubKeys)
expected_values_source.note: 79 published vectors in total (7+12+6+10+7+14+8+15). The 32-character table (qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l) was transcribed from the BIP-173 table in the fetched text and the generator constants 0x3b6a57b2 0x26508e6d 0x1ea119fa 0x3d4233dd 0x2a1462b3 and 0x2bc830a3 from the fetched BIPs. The published reasons are mapped to error classes by a table in the program (for example both 'Invalid data character' and 'Invalid character in checksum' map to 'bad character'); the BIPs give the reasons as prose, and the order in which checks are applied is my choice.

negative_control: built with -DNEG=1 (Bech32m final xor 0x2bc830a2) 0 of 7 valid Bech32m strings are accepted, 3 of 8 BIP-350 segwit addresses decode correctly and 9 of 15 invalid ones get the published reason; with -DNEG=2 (one generator constant off by one) no valid string of either variant is accepted (0 of 7 and 0 of 7) and the program exits 1
not_checked: the checksum design claims of BIP-173 and the appendix of BIP-350 (detection of up to 4 substitution errors, the choice of the constant by search over error patterns)
error correction (the BIPs only specify detection here), the 'q' insertion weakness analysis
segwit script semantics, Base58Check addresses, other networks' human-readable parts
speed (emulator run time says nothing about real hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, accepts and rejects the Bech32 and Bech32m strings and segwit addresses exactly as the BIPs' 79 published test vectors say. It does not show the checksum has the claimed error-detection strength.
